description.en: The United States Judo Federation's recommended junior pathway for judoka aged 16 and under: eleven kyu grades from white to purple belt, then Shodan. Each grade covers personal development, vocabulary, history, rules and technique, with shime waza and kansetsu waza added at the older ages.

note.en: The federation's junior pathway is set out in two documents: the junior section of the Rank Requirement Recommendations Handbook (5/1/21) and the newer junior rank requirements chart (9/22/23). Both describe the same eleven kyu grades and Shodan with the same belt colours, so they are one scheme, and the 2023 chart is transcribed as the current requirements. The chart is a grid of rows (personal development, general concepts, vocabulary, history, rules, tachi waza, osae waza, shime waza, kansetsu waza, kata) by rank; each non-empty cell becomes a section, each printed bullet an item, and an indented sub-list is joined to its heading after a colon, separated by commas. Cell headings are kept at the start of the item they introduce, or as an item of their own where a bulleted list follows. The line printed once above the tachi waza row, "Judoka must be able to name, demonstrate and define each techique", is repeated at the head of each grade's tachi waza section. Three cells in the Yonkyu column are cut off at the cell edge in the chart and are transcribed as far as they print ("Expand physical fitness and", "Continued dojo level refere", "Continue to expand osae wa"). The chart prints "Age Appropriate if over 12" and "Age Appropriate for 14 and up" in the Gokyu column only, although its shime waza and kansetsu waza content begins at Adv Sankyu. The chart gives no minimum ages or class counts, so those are kept from the handbook's junior section, in a section labelled as coming from it. The two documents differ throughout: the handbook's junior section allocates the techniques differently (for example O soto-gari, Deashi-barai and Ippon Seoi-nage at Jukyu, where the chart has o goshi and uki goshi), sets shime waza from 13 and kansetsu waza from 17 where the chart says 12 and 14, spells the 7th grade "Nankyu" where the ranking table has Nanakyu, and repeats the senior Shodan requirements for junior Shodan. Item text is as printed, including the chart's slips ("compeition", "transitinal", "techique", "Enchanced", "philisophy", "cother", "hikkomi gaeshi", resolved to Hikikomi-gaeshi). The chart names grades by the Mon system (Rokkyu, Advanced Rokkyu and so on); labels here give the handbook's rank name with the Mon name in brackets. The handbook's ranking table also lists a Traditional Junior column (White, Yellow, Orange, Green, Blue, Purple for Rokkyu to Ikkyu) with no requirements of its own, so it is not a separate scheme here. "morote-jime", "sankaku gatame" under osae waza and "mawari ashi" are left unresolved.

beltNote.en: The handbook prints each in-between grade as a two-colour belt, for example White/Yellow, or under the Mon system as the lower colour with a stripe of the higher; either is allowed.
